sermon.title: Independence Day
sermon.speaker: Michael Silla
sermon.summary: A family-oriented Independence Day message on sacrifice. America’s founders and soldiers sacrificed for our freedom, and God gave his only Son. Believers offer the sacrifice of praise, lifted hands, doing good, tithes and offerings, and present themselves a living sacrifice—growing from empty to complete, without blemish.
sermon.transcript_source: This transcript comes from YouTube’s automatic English captions, which supply the timing and the words. Punctuation, capitalization and paragraphing were added from the speaker’s pauses and then corrected by hand, and obvious caption errors (names, Bible references) were fixed; his wording was not rewritten. “[unclear]” marks a word or name that was not clear. Editor notes: Delivered by a speaker other than Pastor Kincer (likely Michael Silla—confirm). Includes the national anthem sung by the congregation. Points to check: John Hart’s story (doghouse, death before war’s end); Hebrews 13:15 spoken as “here is 13 15”; Leviticus 3:1 paraphrased. Sensitive content: none notable.

faqs.question: Who was John Hart?
faqs.answer: A farmer with 13 children who signed the Declaration of Independence.

faqs.question: What did God give according to John 3:16?
What was the biggest sacrifice of all?
What is the fruit of our lips?
What does Malachi 3:10 tell us to bring?
faqs.answer: All the tithes into the storehouse.

faqs.question: What does God want to do in us?
faqs.answer: Get us from empty to full.
